subject: Clarifying support access, retention, and emergency (break-glass) procedures
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — support access, retention, and emergency procedures

Hi Liam / Priya —

Thanks for the conversation this morning. Quick recap and clarifying notes so we can keep momentum on the procurement side:

1) Data scope and residency
- FinBridge confirmed only transaction metadata and tokenized card references will be sent to Redwood for inference. No PANs or raw cardholder data will be transmitted.
- You asked about region lock: we support US-only hosting and can pin your model instances to the us-west-2 region for both runtime and log storage.

2) Retention and logging
- By default we retain request/response logs for 30 days. We can offer a customized retention profile (e.g., 7/30/90 days) in the contract and expose a self-serve retention config in the console.
- Audit logs (agent/user actions, admin role changes) are exportable via S3 with daily rollover.

3) Access controls & support access
- Role-based access (fine-grained RBAC) supports: Viewer, Developer, Operator, Security Admin, Support (restricted).
- Support access is off by default; when enabled it creates a time-limited support role token tied to an incident ticket. Support sessions are logged and require an explicit approval workflow (manager approval + ticket ID).

4) Break-glass / emergency access
- We support break-glass with multi-party approval (two internal approvers + customer approver if requested). Access is time-boxed, fully logged, and files a mandatory post-incident report.

Next steps (proposed):
- I attached a short RBAC snapshot and a retention matrix you can use to confirm policies internally.
- Can you confirm: (a) desired retention windows (7/30/90?), (b) whether FinBridge requires customer-side approval for any break-glass events, and (c) whether you want support access enabled for the initial onboarding period?

I'll loop in Ben on the security evidence doc once you confirm.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(rachel.kim@redwood.ai)

Attachments: redwood-rbac-snapshot-20270410.pdf (PDF), retention-matrix-templates.xlsx (XLSX)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finbridge.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@finbridge.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — support access, retention, and emergency procedures

Rachel —

Thanks for the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Retention: leaning toward 30 days for request/response logs, but we need 7 days for payload-level retention in the testing environment. Can you confirm separate retention per environment?
- Break-glass: FinBridge policy requires customer-side approval for any access to production-derived logs. That means we need an API-based approval step or an out-of-band confirmation (we prefer API).
- Support access: enable for onboarding (first 30 days) but limited to non-production only; support in prod should be strictly break-glass with customer approval.

Also, can you provide a short example of the support session log format? Security will want to map fields to our SIEM.

—Liam
Head of Platform Security, FinBridge
liam.oconnor@finbridge.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@finbridge.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — support access, retention, and emergency procedures

Liam —

Appreciate the quick responses. Short answers below and attached a sample support-session.log snippet that maps to common SIEM fields.

- Retention per environment: yes — retention is configurable per environment (production, staging, test). We'll include environment tags on every log entry so you can set granular lifecycle policies.
- Break-glass approval: we support an API-based approval flow (token exchange) that can be configured to require a customer-signed approval callout. I added a related link to the operational runbook (internal) and we'll provide an API contract in the SOW.
- Support access policy for onboarding: we will enable support for non-prod for the 30-day onboarding window. Prod support will require the break-glass workflow and your API approval.

Sample of fields in the support session log (attached file shows a 10-line example):
- session_id, agent_id, requested_resource, start_ts, end_ts, approver_ids, justification, ip_address, actions_performed, artifacts_downloaded

Action items for us: Ben will prepare SOC2-aligned evidence (config screenshots + audit export) and Marissa will draft the SOW language about retention and break-glass API.

Can you confirm by EOD Monday if FinBridge prefers the API flow (token exchange) or still needs email-based approval? That will determine how we scope the SOW.

Thanks,
Rachel

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@finbridge.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — support access, retention, and emergency procedures

Liam / Team —

Following up with the security evidence we discussed. Attached is the RBAC snapshot (roles + scope matrix) and a very small sample of the support-session.log export schema. A couple of practical notes from an operations perspective:

- Least-privilege enforcement: we can bind ephemeral support tokens to a subset of model endpoints and to specific S3 prefixes. That prevents broad access during onboarding.
- Break-glass auditability: all break-glass grants automatically create a tamper-evident record and trigger an alert in the customer-facing audit stream. We can forward those alerts into your SIEM (via syslog or S3 ingestion).
- SLAs: enabling support in non-prod does not change the SLA for production. Any production-level support will need the break-glass flow to be enabled in the contract.

I'll wait for confirmation on API vs email approval. If you pick API, Marissa and I will draft the API schema and a short runbook for your platform team.

Ben
Director, Product Security Ops, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-rbac-snapshot-20270410.pdf, support-session-log-example.txt
